raw_response:
I’m farming the same 20 mu in wheat-maize rotation, so I won’t split the land this year. Wheat is still my main steady crop, and maize follows right after, same as usual. I only studied to middle school, so I don’t do fancy calculations, but I do look at what happened in my own fields and what the better farmers nearby are doing. Last year the wheat did better when I didn’t cut fertilizer too much, especially with one topdressing at jointing, so this year I’ll keep that approach. But fertilizer, water, and labor all cost money, and with some people working off-farm, I can’t manage things too finely. So I’ll stay with a familiar plan: normal sowing dates, improved seed from the local dealer, fertilizer in 2 splits, and irrigation mainly at the key stages. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and plant quickly after harvest. If rains are decent, I won’t push extra irrigation, because pumping from the well is expensive. I’d rather spend enough to avoid a bad yield drop than save too much and regret it later.
